1: # Tasks — flotilla-dash
2: 
3: > **Design-first, then build under the autonomous workflow, PHASED.** Phase 0
4: > produces the design + spec + this task plan and runs the review trio
5: > (systems-review + open-code-review + STORM). Clearing the trio is the bar to
6: > proceed to implementation (operator directive 2026-06-18). The build is phased
7: > in RISK ORDER — read before write, harmless before privileged — with a
8: > `phase-checkpoint` at each boundary (the phase plan is NOT blanket authorization
9: > for all phases; Phase N+1 is re-confirmed at the Phase N boundary).
10: 
11: ## Phase 0 — design + review (this change)
12: 
13: - [x] 0.1 Proposal (`proposal.md`): why, what changes, capabilities, impact, and
14:       the relationship to #102 (reporting) / #103 (deferred tracker abstraction) / #106.
15: - [x] 0.2 Design (`design.md`): the reader + thin-action-proxy architecture, the
16:       read model over existing watch/roster/cos/backlog artifacts, the cnc read
17:       surfaces, the control actions over the confirmed-delivery library, the native
18:       GitHub-backed tracker (single backend, minimal seam), the fail-closed security
19:       posture, the stdlib frontend/SSE transport, phasing, alternatives, open questions.
20: - [x] 0.3 Spec delta: new `dash` capability (`specs/dash/spec.md`).
21: - [x] 0.4 `/systems-review` + `/open-code-review` + `/storm` on the design; iterate to clean.
22:       ROUND 1: systems-review = REQUEST CHANGES (P1 cross-process pane race; P2 DNS-rebinding;
23:       P3 gh identity/error + stale-vs-live); OCR = CLEAN (nits: citation, omitempty, positioning);
24:       STORM = NEEDS CHANGES B+ (B1 "no CSRF by construction" false; B2 rebinding; B3 PaneMutexes
25:       cross-process; B4 SSE auth; B5 gh injection/repo-pin; B6 token-in-ps; B9-11 UX). ALL folded in
26:       (design §3 three-state, §4 stale-vs-live + dash→ledger, §5 NEW cross-process lock, §6 gh hygiene,
27:       §7 browser-attacker defenses + SSE cookie + token provenance, §8 SSE hub mechanism; spec: 5 new
28:       requirements/scenarios). STORM's "read-only tracker" fork DECLINED — operator explicitly
29:       prioritized the native tracker; not re-litigating a decided scope (folded the coupling concerns
30:       as gh hygiene instead).
31: - [ ] 0.4b Re-run the trio on the revised design to confirm clean (round 2).
32: - [ ] 0.5 Report trio-clean to the operator's XO; proceed to Phase 1 under the autonomous
33:       workflow. No genuine fundamental fork surfaced (the one "fork" the trio raised contradicts an
34:       explicit operator directive, so it is decided, not open).
35: 
36: ## Phase 1 — dash server + read cnc (zero blast radius)
37: 
38: - [ ] 1.1 `cmd/flotilla/main.go`: add the `dash` switch arm + usage block.
39: - [ ] 1.2 `cmd/flotilla/dash.go`: flags (`--roster`, `--snapshot-file`, `--ack-file`,
40:       `--bind` [default `127.0.0.1:<port>`], `--auth-token`/`$FLOTILLA_DASH_TOKEN`,
41:       `--repo` for the tracker), default-path resolution mirroring `status` EXACTLY.
42: - [ ] 1.3 `internal/dash`: the read model — load snapshot (`watch.LoadSnapshot`),
43:       ack age, roster bindings (`Config.Bindings()`), CoS ledger, backlog (`backlog.Parse`).
44:       Pure functions, unit-tested with in-memory artifacts + a pinned clock.
45: - [ ] 1.4 `internal/dash`: the HTTP server (`net/http` + `ServeMux`), `embed.FS`
46:       assets, `html/template` page render, `/api/status` (the `flotilla status --json`
47:       SUPERSET), `/api/topology`, `/api/history` JSON endpoints.
48: - [ ] 1.5 `internal/dash`: SSE `/events` hub — ONE shared poller keyed on
49:       `(mtime,size)` of snapshot/ledger/backlog; per-client register/deregister on
50:       disconnect (`Request.Context().Done()`); non-blocking fan-out (drop slow clients);
51:       connection cap; `http.Server` read/write/idle timeouts. `/api/status` JSON poll =
52:       fallback + reconcile-on-reconnect read.
53: - [ ] 1.6 Frontend (vanilla JS, no build): fleet board (three-state freshness),
54:       federation topology org chart, coordination history; SSE live-update wiring; dynamic
55:       data via `fetch`ed JSON only (never server-rendered into `<script>`); reuse `site/` CSS.
56: - [ ] 1.7 Loopback bind by default; `Host`-header allowlist on every handler (anti-rebinding,
57:       lands in P1 so the infra exists before writes); the three-state empty board (absent/stale/fresh).
58: - [ ] 1.8 Tests: read-model purity (snapshot → board JSON; topology from bindings;
59:       ledger/backlog parse), the status-superset contract (name/state always; role for XO;
60:       effective surface), the three-state freshness paths, single-fleet (one-binding) topology,
61:       SSE hub (emit on `(mtime,size)` change, client deregister-on-disconnect), `Host`-allowlist
62:       rejection. `go test -race ./...`.
63: - [ ] 1.9 Docs: `docs/dash-runbook.md` (start, bind, what it reads, no-snapshot note);
64:       README roadmap line. Cold-test the runbook's commands.
65: - [ ] 1.10 `/systems-review` + `/open-code-review` + `/storm` on the Phase 1 diff; iterate clean.
66: - [ ] 1.11 **Phase-1 checkpoint:** report what landed / what's deferred / proposed Phase 2.
67: 
68: ## Phase 2 — native GitHub-backed issue tracker
69: 
70: - [ ] 2.1 `internal/dash/tracker`: a minimal Go interface (`List/Get/Create/Comment/Label/Close`)
71:       with ONE `gh`-backed implementation; parse `gh … --json <explicit-fields>` (pinned field set);
72:       defensive parse (unparseable/empty → typed error); map gh non-zero/non-JSON exits
73:       (unauthenticated / rate-limited / repo-not-found / network) to typed errors. Inject-a-fake
74:       for tests. NO strategy registry, NO config-selected provider (that is the deferred #103).
75: - [ ] 2.2 `--repo owner/name` resolution PINNED AT STARTUP (default: the dash's working-dir repo, as
76:       `gh` resolves) — never request-derived. Injection-safe invocation: bodies via stdin, `--`
77:       option terminator, issue numbers validated as integers.
78: - [ ] 2.3 Tracker UI: list (open issues + `operator-idea` label), detail (body + comments),
79:       create / comment / label / close forms; close is confirmed explicitly.
80: - [ ] 2.4 Gate issue WRITES behind the auth posture + the browser-CSRF defense (custom header +
81:       Origin check, on loopback too); reads follow the read posture.
82: - [ ] 2.5 Tests: backend against a fake `gh` runner (list/create/comment/close happy + the
83:       gh-down typed-error paths: unauth / rate-limited / repo-not-found); handler auth + CSRF
84:       gating on writes; injection-safe arg passing; over-length / missing-repo errors.
85: - [ ] 2.6 Docs: tracker section in `docs/dash-runbook.md` (gh auth prerequisite, --repo).
86: - [ ] 2.7 `/systems-review` + `/open-code-review` + `/storm` on the Phase 2 diff; iterate clean.
87: - [ ] 2.8 **Phase-2 checkpoint:** report; proposed Phase 3.
88: 
89: ## Phase 3 — cnc control actions
90: 
91: - [ ] 3.0 **(shared-core, coordinate with flotilla-dev)** cross-process pane-transaction
92:       lock in `internal/deliver` (per-pane lock file held across the whole confirmed-delivery
93:       transaction) + a one-line acquire in the detector's context-rotate path. Hardens the
94:       pre-existing `send`-vs-`watch` race. PREREQUISITE for pane-driving control — control is
95:       not exposed until this lands.
96: - [ ] 3.1 `internal/dash`: the three control handlers — route (`surface.Confirm.Submit`
97:       via the `cmdSend` path + `relay.Route` addressing, acquiring the 3.0 cross-process lock),
98:       notify (`discord.Post`), resume (the `flotilla resume` recipe path, per-agent locked +
99:       button debounce) — each returning the library's TYPED outcome; each mirrored to the CoS
100:       ledger with dash provenance (best-effort).
101: - [ ] 3.2 Fail-closed security: non-loopback bind REFUSES to start without a token (startup
102:       validation); control + write endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer` (token) when set,
103:       constant-time compare, token from env/file (warn on `--auth-token`), never logged;
104:       browser-CSRF defense (custom header + Origin) on ALL state-changing requests incl. loopback;
105:       SSE on non-loopback authorized by a short-lived HttpOnly SameSite cookie (no URL token).
106: - [ ] 3.3 Control UI: a route composer (`@desk` aware), an operator-note form, a resume
107:       button on crashed desks; surface each typed outcome distinctly (busy/crashed/unconfirmed…);
108:       a stale-state confirm dialog that restates the desk's live state+age (stale ≠ failure).
109: - [ ] 3.4 Tests: each control handler maps to the right library call and surfaces each typed
110:       error; the 3.0 lock — dash route + watch rotate to the same pane do NOT interleave; auth
111:       gate (loopback token-free vs non-loopback-requires-token; missing/invalid token → 401/403
112:       with no side effect); the fail-closed startup refusal; browser-CSRF rejection on loopback;
113:       dash→ledger provenance entry. `go test -race ./...`.
114: - [ ] 3.5 Docs: control section in `docs/dash-runbook.md` (the trust model, the browser-attacker
115:       defenses, the non-loopback token requirement + SSH-tunnel-to-loopback remote recipe, the
116:       typed outcomes).
117: - [ ] 3.6 `/systems-review` + `/open-code-review` + `/storm` on the Phase 3 diff; iterate clean.
118: - [ ] 3.7 **Phase-3 checkpoint:** report; archive the openspec change when all phases land.
119: 
120: ## Phase 4 — ergonomics (later, optional)
121: 
122: - [ ] 4.1 (Optional) fsnotify for sub-second live updates if stat-poll latency is felt.
123: - [ ] 4.2 (Optional) multi-repo tracker scope.
124: - [ ] 4.3 (Optional) a #102 periodic-digest view (pull); periodic PUSH stays XO/notify-driven.
